cases.prompt: Add a `slugify(title: string): string` helper in a new file src/slug.ts and use it from src/index.ts to build a `postPath(title)` function. Then tell me which commands to run to check the change.

all.why: imports the new module with a .js extension, as NodeNext resolution requires
runs commands with the project's package manager

expectations: The import of the new helper in src/index.ts uses the "./slug.js" specifier, matching the existing "./date.js" import and NodeNext resolution.
The suggested commands use pnpm and include a type check (the typecheck script or tsc --noEmit), lint and tests.
The test command runs Vitest once (for example `vitest run` or `pnpm test -- --run`) rather than leaving it in watch mode, or the reply notes that the plain script watches.

cases.prompt: This webhook handler crashes in production when a partner sends a malformed body. Fix it.

any.why: treats the parsed body as unknown

none.why: does not silence the type with any

expectations: The fix validates the parsed body at runtime instead of trusting the `as PaymentEvent` cast.
It uses zod, which the project already depends on, rather than adding a new validation library or hand-rolling a large checker.
A body that fails to parse as JSON or fails validation gets a 4xx response instead of an unhandled exception.

cases.prompt: Users report that after `importAll` resolves, some rows are still missing from the database and the returned count is often 0. Why, and how do I fix it? Add a test too.

all.why: waits for every save with Promise.all or a for...of loop

expectations: Explains that `forEach(async ...)` starts promises nobody awaits, so the function returns before the saves finish.
The fix awaits every save (Promise.all for parallel or for...of for sequential) and returns an accurate count.
The test is a Vitest test that mocks saveRow and checks that all rows were saved by the time importAll resolves.
The command given to run the test runs once (for example `npx vitest run src/import.test.ts`), not in watch mode.
